META.TITLE: Ledger Alternative — The Air-Gapped Wallet You Can Verify
META.DESCRIPTION: Looking for a Ledger alternative? Locker Protocol turns any offline phone into a free, open-source air-gapped wallet: QR-only signing, no USB, no Bluetooth, nothing to buy, nothing to ship.

HERO.SUBTITLE: A hardware wallet asks you to trust a sealed chip and closed firmware. Locker Protocol asks for nothing: the smart contracts are public and verified on-chain, and the wallet holds no keys at all — sign on a phone that never touches the internet.

WHY.TITLE: Why people look for an alternative
WHY.SUBTITLE: Three dated facts — each documented by Ledger's own public communications.

LEAK.TITLE: Customer database breach
LEAK.DESC: Order data of ~272,000 customers — names, home addresses, phone numbers — ended up public, followed by phishing campaigns and physical threats. Buying a security device created the very data that exposed its owners.

RECOVER.TITLE: Ledger Recover
RECOVER.DESC: A firmware update showed the seed can leave the Secure Element when firmware asks for it. "Keys never leave the chip" became a policy — not a property.

CONNECT_KIT.TITLE: Connect Kit supply-chain attack
CONNECT_KIT.DESC: A compromised Ledger npm library served a wallet drainer inside major dApps for several hours. The attack surface wasn't the device — it was the vendor.

WHY.TRADEMARK: Ledger is a trademark of Ledger SAS, used here only to identify the product being compared. Every fact above links to Ledger's own public communications.

OPTICAL.TITLE: Optical air gap
OPTICAL.DESC: No USB, no Bluetooth, no NFC. Transactions cross as QR codes you can see. There is no hidden channel, because there is no channel.

FREE_SOFTWARE.TITLE: Nothing to trust blind
FREE_SOFTWARE.DESC: The contracts are published and verified on every chain. The extension holds zero key material — there is nothing in the browser worth stealing.

NOTHING_TO_BUY.TITLE: Nothing to buy, nothing to ship
NOTHING_TO_BUY.DESC: Any factory-reset phone becomes the vault. No order, no delivery, no customer database — we cannot leak what we never collect.

KEEP_DAPPS.TITLE: Keep your dApps
KEEP_DAPPS.DESC: The Locker extension is a drop-in Web3 wallet: your existing dApp workflow stays exactly the same, only the signing moves off-line.

HONEST.TITLE: What a secure element does better
HONEST.DESC: A certified secure element resists physical extraction: an attacker who steals the device and owns lab equipment faces a hardened chip. That is a real advantage, and we don't claim otherwise. Our answer is different: against remote attacks — malware, drainers, supply-chain compromises — which cause the overwhelming majority of crypto losses, an optical air gap is stricter than any cable.

MIGRATE.SUBTITLE: Three steps, no purchase, no account.

SECURITY.Q: Is a phone really as secure as a hardware wallet?
SECURITY.A: Against remote attacks — malware, drainers, phishing — an offline phone signing over QR codes is stricter than a USB or Bluetooth device: there is no channel to attack. Against physical lab-grade extraction, a certified secure element keeps an edge; our threat model documents this honestly instead of claiming otherwise.

COST.Q: Do I need to buy anything at all?
COST.A: No. Any phone you already own becomes the vault after a factory reset and airplane mode. No device to order, no shipping, no account — and therefore no customer database to leak.

DAPPS.A: Yes. The Locker extension registers as a standard Web3 wallet (EIP-6963), so dApps detect it like any browser wallet. Your workflow stays the same — only the signature happens on the offline vault, through QR codes.

BREAK.Q: What happens if the phone breaks or is lost?
BREAK.A: You restore from your paper backup: an encrypted QR code printed when you created the vault. With the paper and your password, you recover on any other phone in minutes.

FREE.Q: Why is it free — what's the business model?
FREE.A: The software is free of charge, end to end, and stays that way. The project sells an optional pre-configured hardware vault for those who prefer a dedicated device; the keys and the protocol never depend on it.

NO_KEYS.TITLE: Nothing to steal in the browser
NO_KEYS.DESC: A browser extension can be attacked by malware, a rogue extension or a bad update. Ours holds zero key material, so the worst case stays an inconvenience, never a loss.

CLEAR_SIGN.TITLE: You see what you sign
CLEAR_SIGN.DESC: The offline phone decodes calldata, token approvals and typed data, and shows the real content before you approve. Blind signing simply cannot happen.

KEEP_DAPPS.TITLE: Every dApp keeps working
KEEP_DAPPS.DESC: Standard EIP-1193 and EIP-6963 interfaces: connect buttons detect Locker like they detect MetaMask. Swaps, bridges, mints and signatures work unchanged, on 9 EVM chains.

FREE.TITLE: Free, with no account and no server

SEED.Q: Can I import my MetaMask seed phrase?
SEED.A: You can, but we recommend the opposite: create a fresh wallet on the offline phone and transfer your funds to it. A seed that has ever lived on a connected machine may already be compromised, and keeping it defeats the point of an air gap.

DAPPS.A: Yes. The extension exposes the same standard interfaces as MetaMask (EIP-1193, EIP-6963), so dApps list it like any other wallet. Transactions signed from the vault are accepted by DEXes, bridges and exchanges on mainnet.

LOSE.Q: What if I lose the offline phone?
LOSE.A: Your funds are safe. Restore the encrypted paper backup on any other phone with your password. Without both the paper and the password, the phone alone reveals nothing.

COST.A: Nothing. The extension and the vault are free, with no account and no subscription. The project sells an optional pre-configured device for those who prefer dedicated hardware.

META.TITLE: The Locker Protocol Threat Model
META.DESCRIPTION: What Locker Protocol protects against, what it doesn't, and why we chose verifiability over trusted hardware. An honest threat model for air-gapped, QR-only self-custody.

HERO.TITLE: The Locker Protocol Threat Model
HERO.SUBTITLE: What we protect against, what we don't, and why we chose verifiability over trusted hardware.

AIR_GAP.TITLE: Air gap by construction, not by policy
AIR_GAP.DESC: The signing device has no USB, no Bluetooth, no network. Requests and signatures cross as QR codes you can see. A property enforced by physics needs no promise.

VERIFY.TITLE: Verifiable beats certified
VERIFY.DESC: The contracts — where your funds actually live — are published and verified on-chain on all 9 networks. Certification asks for your trust; verified contracts don't need it.

NO_DATA.TITLE: No accounts, no servers, no data
NO_DATA.DESC: Nothing to register, nothing shipped, nothing stored about you. A database that doesn't exist cannot leak.

MALWARE.HOW: Keys live on a device with no network connection. Malware on your computer can propose a transaction — only the offline vault can sign it, after you've read it.

PHISHING.HOW: The vault decodes every request into human-readable fields on a trusted screen before signing. What you sign is what you saw.

SUPPLY.HOW: No hardware is sold, so none can be intercepted. Updates come only through the browser stores, and the contracts holding your funds are verified on-chain.

LOSS.THREAT: Loss or destruction of the device
LOSS.HOW: The paper backup is an encrypted QR code. Print it, store it, restore on any phone with your password.

THEFT.HOW: The vault is encrypted at rest behind your password. But a phone has no certified secure element: against a lab-equipped attacker holding the device, a hardware wallet's chip resists better. On this specific point, a Ledger wins — and we say so.

WRENCH.HOW: No wallet resists physical coercion. The structural answer is M-of-N multisig: no single person, coerced or not, can move the funds.

SE.TITLE: Where a secure element wins
SE.DESC: A certified secure element (CC EAL5+) resists physical key extraction: decapping, glitching, side channels. If your main risk is a sophisticated attacker physically seizing your signer, a dedicated hardware chip defends that scenario better than a phone. We publish this page so you make that trade-off consciously — not discover it later.

WHY_SOFTWARE.TITLE: Why software anyway
WHY_SOFTWARE.DESC: In 2023, Ledger Recover demonstrated that firmware decides what a secure element does: the chip protected the seed only until its vendor shipped a way out. A component you cannot inspect protects you only as long as its vendor chooses to. We prefer properties you can check to promises you must trust.

CREATOR_STORY.TITLE: Why Locker Exists
CREATOR_STORY.CONTENT_P1: Every year, billions of dollars in crypto assets are stolen - not because blockchains are insecure, but because the devices used to sign transactions are compromised. Malware silently alters transaction payloads before they reach your hardware wallet, and by the time you confirm, it's already too late.
CREATOR_STORY.CONTENT_P2: Existing solutions all share the same critical flaw: they require a direct connection (USB, Bluetooth, or software bridge) between the signing device and an internet-connected machine. That connection is the attack surface.
CREATOR_STORY.CONTENT_P3: Locker was built from the ground up to eliminate that single point of failure. By physically isolating the keystore via a true Air-Gap and verifying exact transaction payloads on a completely offline device, it ensures that even on a fully compromised computer, attackers cannot alter or intercept your signatures.
CREATOR_STORY.CONTENT_P4: The smart contracts are 100% open-source. Clone them, audit them, deploy them yourself. No trust required - only math.

FAQ.TITLE: Frequently Asked Questions
FAQ.A1: Locker Protocol is a complete, free ecosystem to secure your crypto. It combines locking Smart Contracts (by time or price condition) with an air-gapped offline Vault compatible with Web3. Each user deploys their own contract - no proxy, no admin key - and remains 100% owner.
FAQ.A2: Yes, 100% free and open-source. Deploying your Locker, the Vault application and the interface are entirely free. The only costs are standard blockchain network gas fees. No platform fees, no subscription, no percentage taken from your assets.
FAQ.A3: The Vault is an application installed on a dedicated device kept permanently offline (Airplane Mode). Your private keys are generated and stored locally, never exposed to the Internet. Communication with the online app is done exclusively via QR codes - no USB, Bluetooth or WiFi.
FAQ.A4: Beyond classic time-based locking, Locker Protocol integrates with Uniswap V2/V3 on-chain oracles. You can create a conditional lock: your tokens only unlock when the market price reaches a defined target. The smart contract checks liquidity pools in real time.
FAQ.Q5: Do I need a dedicated device for the Vault?
FAQ.A5: For maximum security, yes - an old reset smartphone or tablet is enough. You install the Vault, switch to Airplane Mode, and the device stays permanently offline. For testing, you can also use it on your main machine.
FAQ.A6: You define an M-of-N threshold: for example 2 out of 3 signers must approve each action. Signatures are collected offline via QR codes. Once the threshold is reached, any wallet can submit the transaction and pay gas once for the entire group.
FAQ.Q7: What happens if I lose my offline device?
FAQ.A7: When creating the wallet, a 12 or 24-word recovery phrase is provided. Write it on paper and store it safely. If your device is lost or destroyed, install the Vault on a new offline device and import your phrase - all your keys are restored.
FAQ.Q8: What happens if your site shuts down?
FAQ.A8: The interface is just a façade to interact with the blockchain. It holds no funds and no keys. All code is open-source on GitHub: download it, run it locally, and regain full access to your Locker. Your funds are on the blockchain, not with us.
FAQ.Q9: Can signers be changed after deployment?
FAQ.A9: Yes. The SignerManager contract allows adding, removing signers or changing the security threshold at any time. These administrative actions themselves require multi-signature approval from the current quorum.
FAQ.Q10: What is the encrypted Paper Wallet?
FAQ.A10: The Paper Wallet uses AES-256 encryption protected by your password. Even if someone finds your paper, they cannot read the keys without the password. Scan the printed QR code with a new air-gapped device to instantly restore your wallet.
FAQ.Q11: Do my private keys ever travel via Bluetooth or USB?
FAQ.A11: Never. The Vault uses no Bluetooth, NFC, WiFi, or USB. The only communication method is scanning animated QR codes (BC-UR protocol). No malware can cross this physical barrier.
FAQ.A12: Your air-gapped Vault connects to MetaMask via QR codes. You can interact with any Web3 dApp (Uniswap, Aave, etc.) while maintaining total physical isolation. Private keys never leave the offline device.
FAQ.Q13: If tokens are sent to the contract by mistake, are they lost?
FAQ.A13: No. The protocol includes a Token Rescue function. Authorized signers can recover mistakenly sent tokens via a multi-signature action validated by the quorum.
FAQ.A14: Locker Protocol is 100% EVM-compatible and deployed on: Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Polygon, BNB Chain, Avalanche and Linea.
FAQ.A15: Yes. The entire codebase - Solidity Smart Contracts, PWA web interface, and Vault cryptographic modules - is published as open-source on GitHub. Any expert can analyze every line of code.
